summary: Aermotor MC-39 tower on Kaibab NF's Skinner Ridge, erected 1929 or 1933; moved to Encino, NM, in 1950; ridge site listed as gone.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot steel cab
facts.status_note: Ridge site listed as gone; the tower was obtained by the Santa Fe National Forest and erected at Encino, New Mexico, in July 1950
facts.agency: Kaibab National Forest (original site); Santa Fe National Forest, Coyote Ranger District (Encino)
facts.height_note: 59 feet (about 18 m) is the height the 2020 report gives for the Encino tower, where it was re-erected in July 1950

notes_for_editor: The Skinner Ridge build year is 1929 or 1933 per the 2020 report; the brief's 1929 is kept as the first-listed date. Height 59 feet (about 18 m) is the figure for the tower as it now stands at Encino. No staffing, fire or access information for the ridge site was found, so none is recorded. The 2016 Tusayan East decision covers a tower on the ridge, but no source read confirms it was built; check the project documents or recent imagery before saying anything stands there. The 1941 standing and Barbara Zinn's document are known only through the 2020 report. Encino's current status rests on a 2020 source; newer confirmation is worth finding before publishing.
